title: Pick's Theorem via Primitive Triangulation + GCD Boundary Count (S1 OBSERVE)
description: S1 OBSERVE for the open question of whether Pick's theorem (Area = I + B/2 - 1) can be derived in Lean by combining (a) the primitive-triangulation result of PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01 (every lattice triangle decomposes into exactly |det| primitive sub-triangles) and (b) the GCD boundary-count formula of PicksTheoremOQ02 (the segment from (0,0) to (a,b) has gcd(a,b)+1 lattice points). This file scaffolds the bridge data structures, proves the algebraic identity 2·pickInterior = 2A - B + 2, and verifies the bridge formula on three concrete triangles (unit, 2-by-1, 3-by-3).

overview.historicalContext: Pick's theorem (Georg Alexander Pick, 1899) computes the area of a lattice polygon by counting interior and boundary lattice points: A = I + B/2 - 1. The classical proof has two ingredients. (1) Primitive triangulation: every lattice triangle decomposes into |det T| sub-triangles, each of area 1/2. (2) GCD boundary count: the lattice points on the segment from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) number gcd(|x2-x1|, |y2-y1|) + 1. Both ingredients are independently verified in this project (PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.lean and PicksTheoremOQ02.lean, respectively). The open question asked whether they compose into a Lean-formalized Pick's theorem. The answer is yes in principle; this S1 OBSERVE scaffolds the bridge.
overview.problemStatement: Bridge data: for a lattice triangle T = ⟨v1, v2, v3⟩ with vi : ℤ², define twiceArea(T) = |det(T)| where det is the 2D cross product (v2 - v1) × (v3 - v1); boundaryCount(T) = gcd(|Δx_01|, |Δy_01|) + gcd(|Δx_12|, |Δy_12|) + gcd(|Δx_20|, |Δy_20|) summed over the three edges; pickInterior(T) = twiceArea/2 - boundaryCount/2 + 1 (Pick's formula for I). Goal: prove pickInterior T agrees with the true number of interior lattice points of T, by induction on the primitive-triangulation count |det T|.
overview.proofStrategy: S1 OBSERVE establishes the data-level bridge: mirror the LatticeTriangle structure, define twiceArea / edgeGCD / boundaryCount / pickInterior / pickInteriorNum, prove the cleared-denominator identity (Section III), and verify the formula on three small examples (unit triangle (I=0,B=3,2A=1), 2-by-1 triangle (I=0,B=4,2A=2), 3-by-3 triangle (I=1,B=9,2A=9)). The remaining work for future sessions: (S2) define the true interior-point count; (S3) prove pickInterior agrees with it on primitive triangles (base case); (S4) prove the additivity lemma for primitive sub-triangles sharing an edge; (S5) close the induction via PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.exists_primitive_triangulation.
keyInsights: Both ingredients are already verified in the project: PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01 (primitive triangulation, 11 theorems, 0 axioms) and PicksTheoremOQ02 (GCD boundary count, 13 theorems, 0 axioms). The remaining work is purely compositional — wire them together.

Pick's formula has two natural forms. The rational form pickInterior = (twiceArea - boundaryCount)/2 + 1 is cleanest as a definition but introduces division by 2. The cleared form pickInteriorNum = twiceArea - boundaryCount + 2 stays in ℤ and is much easier for inductive proofs. The identity 2·pickInterior = pickInteriorNum is the bridge between them.

Boundary count via GCD has a subtle endpoint-sharing accounting: each edge has gcd(|Δx|, |Δy|) + 1 lattice points, but a triangle's three vertices are each shared between two edges. So B = Σ (gcd + 1) - 3 = Σ gcd. This is why boundaryCount is defined as the bare sum of three GCDs (no +1, no -3).

The bridge requires translation invariance of the GCD count: PicksTheoremOQ02 only handles segments from (0,0) to (a,b) with a, b : ℕ, but a triangle's edges can be in any direction. The reduction to the canonical form uses translation (subtract endpoints) and reflection (take absolute values of differences), both of which preserve GCD.

The remaining mathematical content is the additivity step: when two primitive triangles share an edge, the interior count of the union equals the sum minus the shared-edge interior count. This is where the GCD count interacts non-trivially with the triangulation structure.

sections.title: Imports and Module Docstring
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib.Data.Int.GCD, Mathlib.Data.Nat.GCD.Basic, Mathlib.Tactic. The module docstring lays out the bridge from PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01 (primitive triangulation) + PicksTheoremOQ02 (GCD boundary count) to Pick's theorem, and explains the S1 OBSERVE scope (bridge data + algebraic identity + three concrete examples).

sections.title: Mirror Definitions (LatticeTriangle, det)
sections.summary: Re-declares LatticeTriangle (structure with v1, v2, v3 : ℤ²) and LatticeTriangle.det (the 2D cross product = twice the signed area) in this namespace. Adds LatticeTriangle.NonDegenerate (det ≠ 0). Keeping the file self-contained avoids cross-file import cycles.

sections.title: Bridge Data Structures
sections.summary: Defines twiceArea (= |det T|), edgeDelta i (the pair (|Δx_i|, |Δy_i|) for edge i), edgeGCD i (the GCD), boundaryCount (sum over three edges), pickInterior (Pick's formula as a rational), and pickInteriorNum (cleared-denominator integer form). Edges indexed 0:v1→v2, 1:v2→v3, 2:v3→v1.

sections.title: Algebraic Bridge Identity
sections.summary: Proves two_mul_pickInterior (2 · pickInterior T = pickInteriorNum T, the bridge between rational and integer forms) and pick_formula_cleared (twiceArea = 2·pickInterior + boundaryCount - 2, the cleared form of Pick's formula). Both proofs use push_cast + ring.

sections.title: Test Triangle 1: Unit Right Triangle
sections.summary: Verifies unitTriangle = ⟨(0,0), (1,0), (0,1)⟩ has twiceArea = 1, boundaryCount = 3, pickInterior = 0, pickInteriorNum = 0. All via native_decide + norm_num. Pick's formula 0 + 3/2 - 1 = 1/2 = Area ✓.

sections.title: Test Triangle 2: 2-by-1 Right Triangle
sections.summary: Verifies triangle_2_1 = ⟨(0,0), (2,0), (0,1)⟩ has twiceArea = 2, boundaryCount = 4, pickInterior = 0. Pick's formula 0 + 4/2 - 1 = 1 = Area ✓. (Interior point count is 0 — the (1,0) midpoint sits on the boundary, not the interior.)

sections.title: Test Triangle 3: 3-by-3 Right Triangle
sections.summary: Verifies triangle_3_3 = ⟨(0,0), (3,0), (0,3)⟩ has twiceArea = 9, boundaryCount = 9, pickInterior = 1. Pick's formula 1 + 9/2 - 1 = 9/2 = Area ✓. (The unique interior lattice point is (1,1); the boundary points are (0,0), (1,0), (2,0), (3,0), (0,1), (0,2), (0,3), (2,1), (1,2) — total 9.)

sections.title: Cleared-Form Sanity Checks
sections.summary: Three corollaries unitTriangle_pick_cleared / triangle_2_1_pick_cleared / triangle_3_3_pick_cleared apply pick_formula_cleared to each test triangle, plus three pickInterior_nonneg lemmas confirm the formula does return a non-negative value (i.e., a valid interior-point count) for each case.

conclusion.summary: S1 OBSERVE scaffolds the bridge between primitive triangulation (PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01) and the GCD boundary-count formula (PicksTheoremOQ02): 9 bridge definitions (LatticeTriangle, det, NonDegenerate, twiceArea, edgeDelta, edgeGCD, boundaryCount, pickInterior, pickInteriorNum) and 16 lemmas (one algebraic identity, two cleared-form lemmas, and 13 concrete-triangle verifications). Sorry-free, 0 axioms, 279 lines.
conclusion.implications: The bridge data structures and algebraic identity are now available for future sessions to plug primitive-triangulation and GCD-boundary results into. The cleared-denominator form pickInteriorNum = twiceArea - boundaryCount + 2 is the natural target for an inductive proof: each primitive triangle contributes (1, 3, 0) to (twiceArea, boundaryCount, pickInteriorNum), and the additivity step preserves Σ pickInteriorNum modulo the shared-edge correction.
openQuestions: S2: Define the true interior-point count for a lattice triangle (using Mathlib's Set.Finite or Finset.image over a bounded range of ℤ²) and prove it agrees with pickInterior on the unit triangle (i.e., the base case).

S3: Prove the additivity lemma: when two lattice triangles T1, T2 share an edge with no interior lattice points (i.e., the edge has gcd = 1), the interior counts satisfy interiorCount(T1 ∪ T2) = interiorCount T1 + interiorCount T2.
S4: Close the induction by combining PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.exists_primitive_triangulation with the additivity lemma to derive Pick's formula for arbitrary lattice triangles.
